problem: The sentence "The EVM changes account state only through state changes that a block finally commits" is circular and a first-time reader may not see what it means.
fix: Say instead: "Execution produces state changes inside a transaction, but they become part of account state only when the block carrying that transaction is accepted."

problem: The sentence says determinism follows from the 256-bit word size ("It is a stack machine with 256-bit words, so the same bytecode gives the same result on every node"). Word size does not cause determinism; the fixed opcode rules do.
fix: Separate the two ideas: "It is a stack machine with 256-bit words. Every opcode has one fixed meaning, so the same bytecode on the same input and state gives the same result on every node."

problem: "Gas already used is not fully returned" is vague and a student may read it as a partial refund. In fact the unused gas left in B's frame returns to the caller and the gas consumed is kept.
fix: "Gas that B consumed is spent and is not refunded; the unused gas left in B's frame returns to the caller."
